dek: A Madison, Wisconsin pick service known for its Green Sheet football newsletter, run by Joe Nelson. Its picks are sold through BigAl.com at $30 a play and through Playbook Sports at $20 a play or $49 for a day pass. Playbook's own report card showed 49 wins, 39 losses and 4 ties over 90 days, and 14 wins and 13 losses over the last 30.

short_answer: Nelly's Sportsline is a long running pick service. BigAl.com says it has worked since the 1990 football season from Madison, Wisconsin, with Joe Nelson as lead handicapper since 2003, and Playbook Sports carries the same service on its roster. Forum posts from 2008 to 2024 show its weekly Green Sheet football newsletter being discussed and traded among bettors. We found no website run by Nelly's itself; you buy through BigAl.com or Playbook.

Its record is not proven. The only log we could open is Playbook's report card, graded by the store that sells the picks: 49 wins, 39 losses and 4 ties (55.68%) over 90 days, 14 wins and 13 losses over the last 30 days, and 11 wins and 9 losses in the last 20 graded plays by our count. It lists package names only, with no line, odds or units. BigAl.com's banner claims such as "#1 NFL Win Percentage the last 365 days at over 60%" come with no log we could open.

If you buy, Playbook's pay after you win option limits what you pay for a losing single pick. BigAl.com states plainly that there are no performance guarantees. Neither covers what you lose on the bets.

guarantee: On Playbook, Nelly's picks are listed among the guaranteed picks. The Picks Policy says that with pay after you win, your card "isn't charged until the game finishes and you show a net profit." Profit is counted at $100 per star and includes the price paid. With the prepaid option you pay 20% less, there is "no refund on pre-paid purchases", and a losing purchase comes back as "Reusable Makeup" tokens. The policy says this guarantee "does NOT apply" to prepaid weekly or monthly subscriptions. We found no loss terms on the $49 day pass.

On BigAl.com there is no guarantee. The refund policy states: "There are no performance guarantees for any of the purchased picks or subscription packages. Refunds will not be provided due to poor predictive performance." Single picks are refunded only if a game is suspended or cancelled, postponed more than four days, has a baseball pitching change after the pick is posted, or had already started when you bought. Those exceptions do not apply to subscriptions.
No option on either site covers what you lose on the bets themselves.

claims_note: Many package names carry a run in the title, such as "60% RUN", "6-3 RUN" or "10-6 RUN". Those numbers are the seller's own description of a recent stretch, not a checked record, and several of those titled plays lost on the Playbook report card.

The two stores describe the start date differently: BigAl.com says active since the 1990 football season, Playbook says the service has been around since the late '80s. RotoWire's page for a handicapper named Eric Timm says he is in his 23rd season as a featured handicapper with Nelly's Sportsline, while BigAl.com names Joe Nelson as lead handicapper. We do not know how the work is split between them.
record: What is independently verifiable: nothing complete. We found no third party log of Nelly's paid picks, no contest standings we could open and no regulator or court record in our searches. Old forum posts include one member's weekly tally of a Green Sheet issue from 2016, which we could not check.

What the sellers publish: Playbook Sports grades its own experts. On 17 Nov 2026 Joe Nelson's report card read 49 wins, 39 losses and 4 ties (55.68%) over 90 days, back to 20 Aug 2026, and 14 wins and 13 losses (51.85%) over 30 days. By our count the last 20 graded plays, from 25 Oct to 15 Nov 2026, went 11-9. Plays whose titles name the NFL or an NFL game slot went 12-8 in the 90 day list by our count. Each entry shows only the date, the package title and W, L or T, with no team, line, odds or units, so profit cannot be worked out.

BigAl.com shows daily results with the pick and price: on 16 Nov 2026 Nelly's went 2-1 (+$900 on BigAl.com's scale), losing Kent State -10.5 and winning Minnesota -2 and a Chargers and Ravens over 38.5. We did not find a full history page for Nelly's on BigAl.com. Both stores earn money from selling these picks.

our_data.text: In this edition no Nelly's Sportsline pick is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Nelly's Sportsline performs.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Nelly's is thin. What exists is forum talk on Sportsbook Review and TheRX from 2008 to 2024, mostly about the Green Sheet newsletter rather than the paid daily picks. Our Reddit search was partial because the archive we use kept timing out.

customers.text: We found about eight relevant forum posts on Sportsbook Review and TheRX between 2008 and 2024, and no buyer reviews of the paid daily picks. A long time newsletter reader on Sportsbook Review in 2020 called the Green Sheet insightful and its author a pro. On TheRX the Green Sheet was in demand: members asked for it in 2022 and 2024, and one remarked that it shows up there only about once every two years. The one record dispute we found is from 2016, when one member said the sheet went 3-0 and another counted 1-6 in college and 2-2-1 in the NFL for the same week. We could not verify either. Nothing we found speaks to the BigAl.com or Playbook picks sold today.

A Sportsbook Review member who said they had bet football for decades listed Nelly's Sportsline among the newsletters they read and wrote that "the green sheet can be very insightful", calling its author a pro. They said they rarely play newsletter picks.

On TheRX one member said the Green Sheet went 3-0 the previous week. Another replied that the issue had 7 college and 5 NFL picks and went 1-6 in college and 2-2-1 in the NFL. Neither posted the issue, and we did not verify either count.

A TheRX member posted a Green Sheet issue's rated NFL picks, from Rating 5 down to Rating 1, along with Nelly's Sportsline NFL systems that carried their own long term records, such as 43-27 since 1983. The post shows how the paper was laid out; it is not a review.
The weekly TheRX newsletter post for football week 13 of 2016 listed Nelly's Green Sheet among the papers shared that week.
A TheRX member asked if anyone wanted to split the cost of the Nelly's Green Sheet so it could be posted in the thread.
Members asked for the Green Sheet again in 2024. The thread's regular poster listed papers still missing that week and joked that the Green Sheet appears there about once every two years.
TheRX's daily service play thread lists Nelly's Sports, and all BigAl.com handicappers, among the services members may not post. The page does not give a reason.

We found no website run by Nelly's itself, no Better Business Bureau profile, no app store listing and no customer testimonials on the BigAl.com or Playbook pages we read. Our Reddit search was partial: the archive's full text search timed out, and our saved Reddit posts held no discussion of Nelly's.

conflicts: BigAl.com and Playbook Sports each sell Nelly's picks and each publish the records and leaderboards used to sell them. The store and the scorekeeper are the same company on each site.

Similar Tuesday night MAC packages were priced $30 on BigAl.com and $20 on Playbook on 17 Nov 2026. We could not tell whether they were the same pick, but a buyer should compare both stores before paying.
BigAl.com's FAQ urges readers to bet at more than one sportsbook and points them to its own sportsbook reviews. That is BigAl.com's business, not Nelly's, but it is the store you would buy through.
strengths: A long history that forum posts back up: bettors discussed and traded the Green Sheet on TheRX in 2008, 2016, 2022 and 2024.
A daily report card on Playbook that shows the losses too, including a 3 loss run from 13 to 15 Nov 2026.
Pay after you win on Playbook's guaranteed single picks, so a losing pick bought that way costs nothing.
Cheap single picks ($20 on Playbook) and free picks with written analysis on BigAl.com let you sample before buying a package.
concerns: No full log with lines and odds. The Playbook report card lists package names and W, L or T only.
Banner claims (#1 NFL win rate over 365 days, 11-2 AFC, top 5 net profit) cannot be checked, and Playbook's own 30 day card was 14-13.
BigAl.com offers no performance guarantee and refunds only for game problems, never for losing picks or subscriptions.
The season by season percentages in the biography, mostly from 2015 to 2021, come with no published picks to check them against.
checklist: Ask Joe Nelson's sellers for every pick of the past 12 months, each with its posted time, line and odds. Titles like "7-1 MAC" are a hot run, not a record.
Count units, not wins. Profit on Playbook is counted at $100 per star, so a winning record on chalk can still leave a bettor short once prices are in.
Know which site you are buying from: a losing Playbook prepaid pick returns makeup tokens, pay after you win charges only on a net profit, and BigAl.com refunds nothing for losing picks.
Record each Nelly's play when it is delivered, together with the line your own book is offering then.
Hold off on a verdict until a few hundred of his picks are logged, because short stretches in college football and basketball swing widely.
faq: It is a real, long running service: BigAl.com and Playbook Sports both carry it, and bettors have discussed its Green Sheet newsletter on forums since at least 2008. We could not verify that its picks win over time, because the only record is a report card graded by the store that sells the picks.
How much does Nelly's Sportsline cost?

On 17 Nov 2026 single picks were $30 on BigAl.com and $20 on Playbook, and a Playbook one day pass was $49. BigAl.com subscriptions ran from $100 for 7 days of baseball or hockey to $2,395 for a year of all sports.
Does Nelly's Sportsline have a verified record?
No. Playbook's report card showed 49-39-4 (55.68%) over 90 days and 14-13 over 30 days on 17 Nov 2026, with package names only and no lines or odds. We found no third party log.

BigAl.com and Playbook name Joe Nelson as the operator and lead handicapper, based in Madison, Wisconsin, with Nelson in the lead role since 2003. RotoWire separately describes a handicapper named Eric Timm as a featured handicapper with Nelly's Sportsline.

It depends on the store. Playbook's guaranteed picks can be bought pay after you win, so you are charged only if the purchase shows a net profit. BigAl.com says there are no performance guarantees and refunds only for cancelled, postponed or already started games.

Forum readers have long valued the Green Sheet as research. For the paid picks, a 55.68% run over 90 days on the seller's own card is above the 52.4% needed at -110, but 92 plays is a small sample, the card shows no odds, and the last 30 days were 14-13. Buy single picks pay after you win if you want to test it.
